system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation (one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A higher cap, with separate, higher caps for material risk areas; preserve full recovery for fraud and other agreed carve-outs. | **Reject 20%; seek at least 50% of price for general warranties and tailored higher caps where diligence supports them**, because 20% may leave material warranty losses unrecoverable. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 deductible basket; only excess over basket recoverable. | A lower de minimis and a tipping basket (recovery from the first dollar once crossed), with suitable carve-outs. | **Counter with AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 150,000 tipping basket**, excluding fundamental, tax, fraud and specific indemnity claims, because a deductible basket makes Buyer absorb the first AUD 250,000. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; Seller says limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer general warranty period and explicit separate periods for tax, fundamental and specific claims; no blanket limitation by implication. | **Seek 24 months for general warranties and express longer periods for tax and specific claims**, because 18 months may be too short for issues to emerge and be quantified. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general cap and time limits. | Separate, materially higher or uncapped exposure for title and capacity, with a long limitation period; title must cover good legal and beneficial ownership and no encumbrances. | **Reject the general regime; seek uncapped title/capacity liability (or a price-level cap) and a 6-year period**, because defects in ownership go to the core of the acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | No express fraud position; Seller says limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Expressly exclude fraud (including fraudulent concealment and relevant party attribution) from caps, thresholds, time bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to the extent legally effective. | **Require an express fraud carve-out from every limitation**, because the Seller’s blanket language could otherwise be argued to restrict remedies for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room (DD-002–DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure against each warranty, with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure. | **Delete general disclosure and retain only adequately particularised specific disclosures**, because the broad reference shifts diligence risk to Buyer without identifying what qualifies each warranty. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | No imputed or constructive knowledge bar; at most, a narrowly defined bar for actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals, subject to fraud and specific indemnities. | **Reject the proposed qualifier and limit any knowledge defence to specifically agreed actual knowledge**, because “discoverable” knowledge would make the broad disclosure regime even more extensive. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent. DD-002 shows ~30% of FY26 revenue; final consent and satisfaction of conditions are absent. | A condition precedent requiring valid written consent and satisfaction/waiver of clause 11.3 conditions before Completion, with termination or other protection if not obtained. | **Make effective consent and conditions a Completion condition, not mere delivery**, because Bluefen represents about 30% of revenue and a consent may be conditional or ineffective. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. DD-003 says not repaid and no final security discharge is included. | Repayment at or before Completion from Seller proceeds, lender payout/release mechanics, and discharge of all security as a Completion deliverable; no post-Completion reliance on Seller. | **Require repayment and release/discharge at Completion, with any shortfall secured or withheld**, because a post-Completion release leaves Buyer exposed to debt and encumbrances. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | Seller says AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are its matter and omits them from funds flow. Disclosure says conditional on Completion and continued employment; payroll tax, super and on-costs unclear. | Clear allocation and funding of bonuses and all associated on-costs by Seller, with no leakage to Buyer or Target; reflect treatment in price/funds flow and obtain payroll confirmation. | **Require Seller to fund or deduct the full bonus cost, including on-costs, at Completion**, because the amounts are triggered by the transaction and are absent from the funds flow. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; DD-004 says transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, with AUD 180,000 open and no payment receipt or assignment. | A specific, uncapped indemnity covering title, ownership, infringement and losses from unavailable/defective SOW3 materials, plus proof of cleared payment and effective assignment before Completion. | **Expand the indemnity and require payment evidence and transfer at Completion**, because the current indemnity does not cure the disclosed uncertainty over whether the Target owns usable project materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller calls DD-006 preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure describes unintended email delivery, potentially ~1,240 records, with access and notification status unknown. | Accurate incident warranties and a specific indemnity; complete investigation, containment and any required notifications/remediation before Completion, with records and ongoing cooperation. | **Treat it as a specific risk, not assumed immaterial: require verified investigation and an indemnity or escrow**, because exposure, access and notification obligations remain unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 characterised as ordinary-course operating costs. DD-008/011 do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Review the underlying contracts and renewal status; ensure any pre-Completion commitments or accrued/unusual costs are properly reflected in price and covered by warranties. | **Do not accept the characterisation without contract-level verification and price treatment**, because the disclosures do not establish whether the renewals create unavoidable post-Completion liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller applies limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance terms to all Claims and says tax/IP are settled under the general regime. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud, with tailored caps, thresholds, periods and remedies; express priority over inconsistent general limitations. | **Add an express category carve-out schedule**, because applying one general regime to unlike risks can unintentionally truncate negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing it holds 100%; says this evidences title. | Independently verify issued capital, legal and beneficial ownership, transfer authority, encumbrances and any competing rights, supported by warranties and Completion deliverables. | **Do not treat the register alone as sufficient; verify title and require clean-transfer assurances**, because the register is evidence of the recorded holder, not a complete assurance of transferable, unencumbered title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranties settled under the general regime. | Negotiate bespoke tax and IP warranties, separate caps/time limits and appropriate specific indemnities, based on diligence and the final SPA wording. | **Keep tax and IP expressly open until agreed in the SPA**, because the Seller’s statement does not resolve the substantive terms or justify applying general limits. |

These are buyer-side negotiating positions based on the supplied extracts, not a review of the full SPA, data room or underlying contracts.
=== END ADVICE ===
